item.title: Integrating Ambitions: Making Evaluations Power Effective NDC Implementation
item.description: Climate change action is failing because countries' climate commitments (NDCs) remain disconnected from national planning, sectoral ministries, and financing mechanisms — requiring integrated monitoring and evaluation systems to transform ambition into measurable, fundable progress.

item.title: Seventy Years After the Birth of AI, the Work Begins
item.description: Seventy years after funding the birth of AI at Dartmouth, The Rockefeller Foundation is partnering with Maryland, Anthropic, and Percepta to prove that artificial intelligence can be harnessed to strengthen government services and bridge the gap between citizens and their institutions.

item.title: Adapt or Fall Behind: Why Climate Data Is Non-Negotiable for Health Resilience
item.description: This blog highlights how climate services are being rapidly integrated into global health systems — especially through Brazil’s Belém Health Action Plan — to protect communities from climate-driven health risks and turn climate-health frameworks into real-world impact.

item.title: How Nuclear Power Can Reduce the Cost of Clean Energy Abundance in Emerging Economies
item.description: Nuclear power can reduce clean energy system costs by 2-31% in developing countries by complementing renewables and dramatically lowering the need for expensive solar capacity, storage, and transmission infrastructure.

item.title: Designing a Better World — Together
item.description: COP30 underscored the urgency of the climate crisis while revealing a clear path forward: climate-smart development, empowered local leadership, and transformed finance systems that integrate adaptation and mitigation to build resilient communities and economies.

item.title: A New Partnership To Embed Learning in Transition Minerals Policymaking
item.description: A new learning platform enables Global South countries to share real-time experiences and co-develop best practices for managing transition mineral resources while protecting communities and driving economic development.

item.title: A New Chapter for Latin America and the Caribbean
item.description: With the opening of its Bogotá office, The Rockefeller Foundation is deepening its long-standing commitment to Latin America and the Caribbean by working alongside local partners to advance people-centered climate action, strengthen livelihoods, and drive lasting regional impact.

item.title: Who Owns the Response To Heat? In Bangladesh, Everyone Does
item.description: After losing 26.5 billion labor hours to heat in 2023, Bangladesh is scaling HeatShield — a first-of-its-kind system helping farmers stay safe in a rapidly warming world.

item.title: Meet the 2025 and 2026 Bellagio Center Residents Transforming the World
item.description: At the Bellagio Center, global leaders turn ambitious ideas into solutions that improve lives — explore the impact of recent residents and apply for the 2027 cohort.

item.title: A Food System for the Future: From School Meals to Food is Medicine
item.description: A look at how Regenerative School Meals and Food is Medicine can reshape food systems to improve health, support farmers, and strengthen communities.

item.title: How Food is Medicine Can Strengthen Farms, Communities, and Health
item.description: From farms to healthcare systems, Food is Medicine is reshaping how we think about health, agriculture, and economic opportunity.

item.title: Another Energy Crisis Is Here. This Time, the Way Out Is Different.
item.description: The largest oil supply shock in history has exposed a critical paradox: clean energy is now the cheapest path to stability, yet the most vulnerable countries still can't afford to build it.
